name: Sakaecho
tagline: Tokyo in 30 minutes and Shinjuku in 34 minutes. Served by 1 line. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥100,000 to ¥110,000.
summary: The station is in Kita City, where the Tokyo Metropolitan Bureau of Transportation run 1 line between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 34 minutes to Otemachi, 34 minutes to Shinjuku, 39 minutes to Shibuya and 44 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥100,000 to ¥110,000. The station stands 4.7 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 21.3 m. The land around the station rises and falls sharply.

terrain.note: The station sits lower than the ground around it, at 4.7 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 3.1 m to 24.4 m, a difference of 21.3 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls inside the projected inundation area, to a projected depth of 0.5 to 3 m. Of the nine points within 400 m of the station, 6 also fall inside the area, and the deepest projection is 3 to 5 m. For storm surge, 3 of the nine points also fall inside the projected area. On the whole, the flood projection here is about average for the 23 wards.

medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 17 clinics and 15 pharmacies. Day-to-day care is available close to the station. The nearest hospital is 桑原病院, about 13 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 愛誠病院, about 32 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 1 line serve the station: Tokyo Sakura Tram (Toden Arakawa Line).
congestion: The ministry's congestion survey does not publish figures for Tokyo Sakura Tram (Toden Arakawa Line). It covers the major commuter stretches, and this line is not among them.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥100,000 to ¥110,000 and 1K ¥100,000 to ¥110,000. 1LDK ¥160,000 to ¥170,000 and 2LDK ¥210,000 to ¥220,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥100,000 to ¥110,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is on the high side. quiet surroundings pushes the figure up. On the other side, only one line, the {line}, serving the station and a climb from the station to much of the housing holds it down. For One room, 2LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.

neighbours.lead: For lower rent, Asukayama; for quiet, Sakaecho.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Sakaecho. It is served by the same lines as Sakaecho. Journey times to the main business districts are much the same. A one-room flat costs about ¥28,000 less at Asukayama. On quiet, Sakaecho comes out ahead.

neighbours.lead: For rail connections, Oji; for quiet, Sakaecho.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Sakaecho. Oji also has the JR Keihin-Tohoku Line and Tokyo Metro Namboku Line, which Sakaecho does not. With more lines, Oji is the better connected of the two. To Toranomon, for instance, Oji is 8 minutes quicker. A one-room flat also costs about ¥19,000 less at Oji. On quiet, though, Sakaecho comes out ahead.

noiseSources: The 首都高速中央環状線 viaduct runs just outside the station. It is an expressway, so traffic is audible day and night

leads.terrain: The ground around the station rises and falls sharply, and living above or below the slope changes how much effort getting about takes.
leads.groceries: There are 13 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 3 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The station itself sits inside the area projected to flood in the heaviest rainfall the government models.
leads.stationNote: Only the Tokyo Sakura Tram (Toden Arakawa Line) serves this station, so when it stops you walk to another station.
leads.rentRange: Set against how long the commute takes, rents here are on the high side.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is among the highest in the 23 wards.
leads.noiseSources: Whether a flat faces the road changes what you hear indoors.
